hero.alt: Green title card reading Wudu With a Pimple Patch

sources.title: Darul Ifta Birmingham fatwa 07322: Wudhu With Makeup
sources.supports: Wudu is invalid if something prevents water reaching the skin of washed parts; makeup usually does not form such a barrier.

sources.title: Darul Ifta Birmingham fatwa 01598: How to do ghusl if an area is covered with a bandage
sources.supports: A hospital patch over a spot with liquid: if the area cannot be washed or wiped, wiping the bandage with wet hands is compulsory for ghusl.

sources.title: Darul Ifta Birmingham fatwa 03049: Bandage wiping and wound healing
sources.supports: Citing Quduri, wiping continues if the bandage falls before healing and stops once healed; if water still causes pain it may be kept covered.

sources.title: Darul Ifta Birmingham fatwa 05471: Pus Coming Out of the Wound
sources.supports: Pus not flowing by itself does not break wudu; a plaster may be used; renew wudu if pus comes out beyond the plaster by itself.

sources.title: Quran 5:6 (Al-Ma'idah), The Clear Quran translation
sources.supports: Command to wash the face for prayer; It is not Allah's Will to burden you.

review.notes: All fiqh claims come from four Darul Ifta Birmingham (Hanafi) fatwas and are attributed as such; the article states other schools were not checked. Applying the barrier principle and the bandage-wiping rule to a pimple patch, and the ghusl-to-wudu extension of fatwa 01598, are explicitly labelled as this guide's reasoning. The makeup fatwa's statement that makeup usually is not a barrier is reported accurately and contrasted with a patch. The question of repeating past prayers is not ruled on and is referred to a local scholar. Quran 2:185 was captured but not used. Abu Dawud 336 could not be retrieved (HTTP 403) and is not cited.

claim_checks.claim: The wudu verse tells believers to wash their faces when they rise for prayer.
claim_checks.explanation: Captured translation: When you rise up for prayer, wash your faces.

claim_checks.claim: Quran 5:6 says It is not Allah's Will to burden you.
claim_checks.explanation: Captured translation contains: It is not Allah's Will to burden you, but to purify you.

claim_checks.claim: Wudu is invalid and incomplete if something prevents water reaching the skin of the washed parts, and makeup usually does not form such a barrier.
For a hospital patch over a spot with liquid, if the area cannot be washed or wiped, one must wipe over the bandage with wet hands for ghusl to be valid.
claim_checks.explanation: Captured question describes a spot with liquid on the leg with a hospital patch; answer says it is compulsory to wipe the bandage with wet hands for ghusl to be valid.

claim_checks.claim: Citing Quduri, wiping continues if the bandage falls before healing and is no longer allowed once healed; if water still causes pain the area may be kept covered.
claim_checks.explanation: Captured answer quotes Imam Quduri to this effect and adds that if there is still pain due to water it may be kept covered.

claim_checks.claim: Pus that does not flow out by itself does not break wudu, a plaster may be used, and wudu is renewed if pus comes out beyond the plaster by itself without pressing.
